title: Central Bank Gold Statistics: Central banks continue summer spree in August
gist: Central banks reported net gold buying of 39t in August 2026 and 170t year-to-date, led by China (20t, 22nd straight month, 648t vs a 700t target), Uzbekistan and Poland, while Turkey and Russia remain net sellers. Seasonal analysis shows only modest patterns, and moves like DNB's 86t transfer to London point to more active reserve management.

insights.claim: Reported central bank net gold buying was 39t in August 2026, taking year-to-date reported purchases to 170t, led by China, Uzbekistan and Poland.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: 170t over eight months is a steady but unspectacular pace; the headline masks heavy concentration in a few buyers.
insights.locator: Global central banks remain on pace

insights.claim: Monthly central bank purchases show only modest seasonality over 2016-2025 (strongest in June and September-October), with large year-to-year differences; the author declines to attribute it to uncertainty without further analysis.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Seasonal timing is a weak trading signal; September-October averages are historically firm but wide error bars limit confidence.
insights.quote: Purchasing activity has tended to be strongest in June and September-October

insights.claim: The WGC argues August's buying reflects multi-year reserve accumulation programmes, with monthly swings driven by implementation, market conditions and liquidity needs rather than changing intent.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Treat dips in monthly prints as noise, not a regime change, for programme buyers.

insights.claim: China's central bank added 20t in August, its 22nd consecutive month of buying, bringing holdings to 648t against a 700t target and 80t added year-to-date.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: If the 700t target is read literally, roughly 52t remains; at 2026's pace that is within about a year, raising the question of what happens after.

insights.claim: Gold is only about 9% of China's total reserves (around 2,387t per the article), leaving large room for further allocation relative to peers such as Uzbekistan at 90%.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The low share implies a long structural runway for Chinese buying even after hitting stated targets.

insights.claim: The WGC notes China is catching up with Poland, the leader in year-to-date purchases at 98t versus China's 80t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: China could overtake Poland as top 2026 buyer within a few months at current paces.
insights.quote: we do see China catching up
insights.locator: The National Bank of Poland continued

insights.claim: Poland bought 8t in August and leads 2026 purchases at 98t; Uzbekistan bought 8t (about 50t YTD, gold 90% of reserves, 439t); Kazakhstan bought 7t (about 36t YTD, 79% of reserves, 377t).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Commodity-exporting Central Asian reserves are now overwhelmingly gold, so their buying is increasingly a policy stance rather than diversification at the margin.

insights.claim: The Czech National Bank has bought gold for 42 consecutive months, holding 86t (7% of reserves) after 14t YTD.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Persistent small-scale buyers add a steady bid that is insensitive to price.

insights.claim: Turkey bought 3t in August after three months of net sales but is net seller of 82t year-to-date, mostly in Q1 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
entities: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
insights.so_what: Turkey is the main offset to 2026 gross buying; a return to buying would lift net totals meaningfully.
insights.locator: The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

insights.claim: Russia's central bank sold another 6t in August, 56t net sold year-to-date, leaving 2,271t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Sovereign sellers are absorbing part of the official-sector bid, so 170t net understates gross demand.
insights.locator: The Central Bank of Russia continued

insights.claim: Jordan sold 3t in August but remains a net buyer of 2t year-to-date, with 75t of gold at about 37% of reserves.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Minor flow, but shows high-gold-share holders still trim at the margin.

insights.claim: Central banks are taking a more active approach to managing gold: De Nederlandsche Bank announced on 2 September it would move 86t from New York and Ottawa to London to improve liquidity and tradability, and Banque de France did a similar operation in 2025.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold is shifting from passive vaulted reserve to a managed, tradable asset, with London strengthened as a hub; this may imply readiness to lend or sell gold when needed.
insights.quote: improving the liquidity and tradability of its gold reserves
insights.locator: Central banks take on fresh approach to gold

insights.claim: Several central banks have reportedly repatriated or relocated gold over the past several years, signalling a broader trend.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Location of custody is becoming a strategic variable alongside quantity.
insights.locator: Central banks take on fresh approach to gold
